turn off verb

a tap

classical

1Not Traupman’s versāre / reversāre (Traupman 123); reversāre is Late Latin. Jack’s ruling, 29 October 2026. Ruling: Turning a tap on and off.

epitonium claudere1

turn the tap off

Examples

  • «Satis est,» inquit. «Siste aquam.» Puer epitonium ipse clausit.

    “That’s enough,” he said. “Turn the water off.” The boy turned the tap off himself.Libellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae

Other words

  • aquam sistere — turn the water off

    also used · classical

See also turn on, tap.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 123, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.
